name: Rogers-Satchell Drift Detector
note: Ratio of the UNdemeaned close-to-close variance (expectation sigma^2 + mu^2) to the Rogers-Satchell range variance (drift-free), so DR-1 estimates (drift/vol)^2 per bar with no smoothing constant. Trades in the direction of the N-bar return sum when DR clears the gate and the close is the extreme of the last few bars; exits when DR collapses back into the noise. From Rogers & Satchell (1991).
source: Rogers & Satchell (1991), 'Estimating variance from high, low and closing prices', Annals of Applied Probability 1(4), 504-512 (the drift-independent estimator); Parkinson (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 61-65; Garman & Klass (1980), Journal of Business 53(1), 67-78. Estimator comparison and formulas: https://portfoliooptimizer.io/blog/range-based-volatility-estimators-overview-and-examples-of-usage/ and https://macrosynergy.com/research/six-ways-to-estimate-realized-volatility/ . The drift-ratio construction itself is my synthesis from those estimators' bias properties.
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    """Two variance estimators of the same diffusion, differing only in how
    they treat drift. Their ratio is the drift-to-noise estimate."""
    import math
    bars = ctx.bars
    m = len(bars)
    n = max(2, int(ctx.p.rs_n))
    o = [float(b["o"]) for b in bars]
    h = [float(b["h"]) for b in bars]
    l = [float(b["l"]) for b in bars]
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]

    lr = [0.0] * m          # log return
    r2 = [0.0] * m          # squared log return -- UNdemeaned on purpose
    rs = [0.0] * m          # Rogers-Satchell per-bar term
    for i in range(m):
        if i > 0 and c[i] > 0.0 and c[i - 1] > 0.0:
            x = math.log(c[i] / c[i - 1])
            lr[i] = x
            r2[i] = x * x
        if o[i] > 0.0 and h[i] > 0.0 and l[i] > 0.0 and c[i] > 0.0:
            v = (math.log(h[i] / c[i]) * math.log(h[i] / o[i])
                 + math.log(l[i] / c[i]) * math.log(l[i] / o[i]))
            rs[i] = v if v > 0.0 else 0.0

    dr = [None] * m
    sr = [None] * m
    s2 = 0.0
    ss = 0.0
    sl = 0.0
    for i in range(m):
        s2 += r2[i]
        ss += rs[i]
        sl += lr[i]
        if i >= n:
            s2 -= r2[i - n]
            ss -= rs[i - n]
            sl -= lr[i - n]
            sr[i] = sl
            if ss > 1e-16:
                x = s2 / ss
                dr[i] = x if x < 100.0 else 100.0
    ctx.dr = ctx.series(dr, "drift_ratio")
    ctx.sr = ctx.series(sr, "ret_sum")


def signal(ctx, i):
    d = ctx.dr[i]
    s = ctx.sr[i]
    if d is None or s is None:
        return 0
    if d < ctx.p.dr_in:
        return 0
    k = max(2, int(ctx.p.conf))
    cc = ctx.c[i]
    hi = True
    lo = True
    for j in range(1, k):
        if i - j < 0:
            break
        p = ctx.c[i - j]
        if p is None:
            break
        if p > cc:
            hi = False
        if p < cc:
            lo = False
    if s > 0.0 and hi:
        return 1
    if s < 0.0 and lo:
        return -1
    return 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    d = ctx.dr[i]
    return d is not None and d < ctx.p.dr_out
